baer-heitev/7:_: From the Torah. In Shlah he extended to side that Parashat Parah is not d'oraisa — so Bach; so in responsum of Maharil siman 182 he mentioned only Parashat Zachor. In Tur HaShulchan siman 108 he wrote: in Ashrei chapter 7 of Berachot he wrote positive mitzvah d'oraisa to read Parashat Zachor with ten; in Tosafot Shantz they wrote no Torah reading is d'oraisa except Parashat Zachor; in Tosafot Ketuvot on Berachot chapter 2 they explained Parashat Zachor and Parashat Parah are obligatory from Torah, etc.; if so one must be more careful that they hear Parashat Zachor on the 14th from Megillah reading in its time — but the world is not careful thus — end. Magen Avraham wrote: it appears to me to resolve world custom — is it written in Torah they must read specifically this Shabbat? Rather Chazal instituted this Shabbat since many are in synagogue near Purim to connect Amalek's action to Haman's action — if so when hearing on Purim Parashat Vayavo Amalek he also remembers Amalek's action and fulfills positive mitzvah; so Raavan siman 2. But Parashat Parah we do not find d'oraisa — end there. Rashal wrote a minor does not ascend as maftir for Zachor and Parah — end. Bach wrote whether minor who knows for whom they bless or does not know — he ascends — end; Taz wrote specifically minor who knows for whom they bless ascends. In siman 282 Rama ruled a minor may read in additional portion or four portions added in Adar — appears when he knows for whom they bless — end there; see Ginat Veradim Orach Chayim klal 1 siman 37. Maharil wrote in all four portions do not mention souls and say tzavtzav dam. Some practice in leap year to establish fast every Thursday from Parashat Sheuvim until Ta'anit Esther; some say also Vayakhel and Pekudei and say Shomer Yisrael, etc. Plain the shaliach tzibbur says its matter in Shacharit and Minchah. Ari z"l wrote in Torah commentary these days are auspicious to repair keri sin more than all year for those fasting — therefore begin from Parashat Shemot when bondage began, repaired through Parashat Ki Sisa when Hebrew slave goes free — end:
beur-hagra/7:א: (א) Seif 7: Some say Parashat Zachor. There: positive mitzvah remembrance, etc., and from what, etc.:
eliyah-rabbah/7:_: [ז] [Levush] Fast in leap year in first Adar, etc. If they did not die in leap year in second Adar, then fast in second in leap year; some are stringent always to fast in both (Levush siman 568), but Rama did not write "always" — implies for all: if died in first or second, fast thus in leap year; so Bach Yoreh De'ah end siman 402 — only if died in simple year some say fast in both as if leap, some dispute first Adar. Magen Avraham siman 568 challenged Ta'anit daf 18a for leap month — Rashi explained leap year, etc. — implies plainly practiced in second Adar; also we say there 18b Tyranos day and Nikanor day all practiced in second Adar — end. In my humble opinion no difficulty: it appears to me it was leap in second Adar — for in Terumat HaDeshen siman 294 he brings proof from fast seventh Adar and fasting in first — he challenged perhaps Moshe died first Adar and needed this proof in simple year — if so same here appears second. Rule: if died in Adar in simple year, fast in leap in first as Levush wrote and Rama in Yoreh De'ah there as practiced; Shach wrote there practiced fasting in both. In my view where no known custom, be stringent for oneself not for others; mourners need not give Kaddish except in first. Terumat HaDeshen wrote in name of Sefer Chasidim: one whose father died first Adar fasted simple year in Shevat and Adar — end. Magen Avraham wrote mourners need give him Kaddish only once — see siman 433 s.k. 2. Magen Avraham there: one whose father died first day of Rosh Chodesh Kislev — next year Cheshvan deficient and Rosh Chodesh Kislev only one day — establish 29 Cheshvan; so Taz wrote; but when first year also full, must establish on Rosh Chodesh — therefore even later deficient years establish Rosh Chodesh — it is like a vow — we follow people's language; see siman 55 s.k. 9. Taz there: if his deceased died on Hanukkah, yahrzeit is not that Hanukkah day but after day of Rosh Chodesh — we follow how many days in month was death day, so yahrzeit — end. What Magen Avraham wrote there if died first day of Rosh Chodesh Adar he fasts, etc. — wondrous — see there.
eshel-avraham/3:_: Parashat Parah — incident they forgot and did not read; he ruled in Tveria on 14th siman 106 that next Shabbat which is Parah they read it too.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (א) [Seif 1] Rosh Chodesh Adar next to Nisan, etc. That it had to say next to Nisan teaches in leap year we do not read in first Adar next to Shevat but in second Adar next to Nisan as in Megillah daf 6b — see there; see reason below siman 697.
machatzit-hashekel/1:א: (א) Magen Avraham wrote: in Shlah he extended in Ashrei chapter 7 Berachot, etc. — he is in siman 20: R' Elazar entered synagogue, found no ten, freed his slave to complete ten; challenged how so — R' Yehuda: whoever frees his slave violates positive command, etc.; public mitzvah is different — as written venikdashti betoch Bnei Yisrael — meaning positive mitzvah to sanctify God's name in ten, even if rabbinic matter such as hearing Kedushah and Barchu, etc. — nevertheless positive commandment of individual is deferred — not reasonable to say it speaks of Torah positive commandment such as reading Zachor which was from Torah — implies in any matter — end.
magen-avraham/1:_: In Shlah he extended to side Parashat Parah is not d'oraisa — so Bach; so in responsum Maharil simanim 182 and 267 mentioned only Parashat Zachor. Tur HaShulchan siman 108: in Ashrei chapter 6 Berachot wrote positive mitzvah d'oraisa to read Zachor with ten; Tosafot Shantz: no Torah reading d'oraisa except Zachor; Tosafot Ketuvot Berachot chapter 2 explained Zachor and Parah obligatory from Torah, etc.; Semag wrote positive mitzvah remember what Amalek did; if so be more careful they hear Zachor on 14th from Megillah in time — world not careful — end; it appears to me to resolve custom — is it written in Torah specifically this Shabbat? Chazal instituted this Shabbat since many in synagogue near Purim to connect Amalek to Haman as Levush — when hearing on Purim Vayavo Amalek remembers Amalek and fulfills positive mitzvah; Raavan siman 2; regarding Parah I hold not d'oraisa — truly no Torah reason for its reading and I do not know where hinted; it appears correct girsa as Chiddushei Rashba: they challenged we do not find Torah scroll reading unless Rashi says reading portions such as Parah and Zachor from Torah — end; nevertheless each should be careful and zealous in mitzvah to come to minyan; Megillah 18 implies plainly Zachor d'oraisa; implies there likewise Vayavo Amalek suffices. Maharil: in all four portions do not mention souls, say tzavtzav (dam). Some in leap year establish fast every Thursday from Sheuvim through Ta'anit Esther; some say also Vayakhel Pekudei, Shomer Yisrael, etc.:
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) They read Parashat Shekalim — Scripture said this is the month's offering in its month for months of the year; the extra lechodshei teaches Torah said you have a month to renew with continual and additional offerings from new terumah — that is Nisan as Gemara learns gezeirah shavah this month is Nisan; since in Nisan must bring from new terumah, we precede and announce shekalim in Adar next to it that they bring shekalim on Rosh Chodesh Nisan; we fulfill with our lips in reading Ki Tisa where shekalim matter is written. Yotzer — for Shacharit and also Musaf on Shekalim and HaChodesh; on Zachor and Parah they did not institute in Musaf [Peri Megadim]. If they did not read the portion of the day — no makeup to next Shabbat [Shaarei Ephraim]. If congregation forgot Shekalim — likewise other three portions — if already said weekly haftarah with its blessings and remembered, must return, take out sefer Torah, read portion with blessing before and after, then Kaddish and maftir without blessings; if remembered after beginning haftarah blessing and will complete the blessing, etc., finish blessing, say some verses of weekly haftarah [so blessing has where to apply] without final blessing, take out sefer Torah, read one aliyah of the day, after final blessing Kaddish and haftarah without before blessings, bless after blessings. If remembered immediately after final blessing on Torah — take another sefer, place by first, Kaddish, then read after maftir of day with blessings [there]. If they erred and read portions and Megillah in first Adar — must return read Megillah in second; regarding portions Beit Yosef implies no return; Darkei Moshe and Eliyah Rabbah wrote must return.
mishnah-berurah/7:ג: (טז) To a place with minyan, etc. — even if he has sefer Torah at home but no minyan at home; even if minyan for Zachor is rabbinic, nevertheless essence of Zachor reading is d'oraisa. Terumat HaDeshen wrote hearing Zachor with ten is preferable to Megillah reading in congregation — most poskim hold Megillah suffices in time alone; if impossible to fulfill both, see to fulfill Zachor in congregation; Magen Avraham sides better come where Megillah read in congregation and Zachor fulfilled with strain hearing Vayavo Amalek on Purim — thereby remembers Amalek and fulfills positive mitzvah — meaning d'oraisa. For what we hold siman 60 mitzvot require intent — he should intend when hearing this portion to fulfill positive mitzvah of Zachor; in my view essence of Magen Avraham requires study — for Torah writes remember what Amalek did, etc., ambushed you, etc., blot out, etc. — intent not to forget what Amalek did and tell children generations saying thus the wicked did and therefore commanded blot his name as Ramban wrote in commentary — this is not mentioned in Vayavo Amalek.
peri-megadim/2:א: (א) Obligated — ATZ brought minor who does not know for whom they bless cannot bless; what he wrote in reading without blessing — perhaps not like blessings do not block, only rabbinically must also bless; perhaps understand holy words of our master z"l light of Israel literally as Ramban z"l in hasagah on counting mitzvot — mitzvah to bless on Torah reading whenever read, for I call upon the Name — see there mitzvah 15; if so blessings do not block rabbinically — blessing from Torah blocks; I also saw z"a: reading in congregation and to bless — already blessed Barchu at day's start, their view for whole day; blessing in congregation rabbinic — requires study. Also Bach: Torah reading from Torah every Shabbat — see above laws of Sukkah implies rabbinic, Moshe instituted himself, from Moshe's words asmachta — no Torah reading except Zachor and Parah; some say all rabbinic — see Magen Avraham; nevertheless all careful. Know if he has minyan to hear Parashat Parah and no Megillah reading there — certainly Megillah preferable even though some say Zachor d'oraisa — already fulfilled Shabbat hearing Vayavo Amalek.
turei-zahav/7:_: Obligated from Torah. Tur HaShulchan siman 108: must be careful reading in congregation more than Megillah reading — although Megillah preferable and every mitzvah deferred before it; per most poskim Megillah read even individually; Parashat Zachor — Ashrei three who ate: positive mitzvah d'oraisa read with ten; defers Torah prohibition always serve them — therefore R' Elazar freed slave to complete ten. Tosafot Shantz: no Torah reading except Zachor; Tosafot Ketuvot Berachot chapter 2: Zachor and Parah obligatory from Torah — end. Rashal feared from this minor does not ascend maftir Zachor — although shaliach tzibbur reads Torah — what of it? we require bar chiyuva to ascend; he also reads Torah — only shaliach reads loud not to embarrass; also Parah be careful since those Tosafot imply d'oraisa; as I found in Chiddushei Mordechai — end; Moharach z"l wrote incorrectly — for minor who knows for whom they bless certainly permitted although minor reads loud — minor counts for minyan of seven; Torah reading every Shabbat d'oraisa from Moshe spoke the appointed times, etc. — Yerushalmi, brought Rif chapter HaKorei Omed — only no fixed order per reading except Zachor; Ezra fixed order for all readings; even minor not knowing for whom they bless — why not fulfill through shaliach tzibbur's Zachor reading — what difference ascending to Torah if minor — primary obligation they hear Torah reading — end his words. In my humble opinion minor not knowing for whom they bless — do not fulfill blessing through him nor reading without blessing — therefore do not call minor maftir not knowing; but knowing — appears they fulfill; siman 282 Rama ruled minor may read additional or four Adar portions — appears when knows for whom they bless.
chokhmat-shlomo/7:_: Seif 7. Some say Parashat Zachor and Parashat Parah Adumah must be read d'oraisa, etc. NB: I was asked by one scholar about what Magen Avraham wrote in this siman that one fulfills through the positive mitzvah of remembering Amalek by what they read as Parashat Vayavo Amalek on Purim — if so, why in Megillah daf 30 do they say that when Purim falls on erev Shabbat they advance Parashat Zachor so that action does not precede remembrance. And how can action precede remembrance — behold one fulfills through Parashat Vayavo Amalek and it is action and remembrance together. And seemingly the questioning scholar asked well. But I answered that in truth let it be settled and it comes out fine: behold it is difficult — if one fulfills through Parashat Vayavo Amalek, why did Chazal enact to read Parashat Zachor first. But the matter is that one who examines Magen Avraham will see his intent is thus: his main wonder against the world is in the view of those who hold Parashat Zachor is d'oraisa — why are they lax in this. And it is implied from his words that if it were d'rabbanan it would not be difficult for him; and likewise he admits afterward that Parashat Parah is also not d'oraisa — it is proven from his words it is not difficult for him only if it were d'oraisa; and therefore he answers thus: there are two matters here — d'oraisa there is a positive mitzvah to remember what Amalek did to you, but it suffices with what mentions the body of Amalek's act, namely Parashat Vayavo Amalek; but Rabanan enacted they also read the parashah of the mitzvah that the Torah commanded in the positive mitzvah to mention Amalek's act — that this parashah too shall be read, as they enacted in Parashat Shekalim and Parashat HaChodesh which are d'rabbanan — so they enacted here to read also the body of the parashah of Zachor; and if so this reading is d'rabbanan. Therefore Magen Avraham answers thus: initially he thought there is no other remembrance for us from Amalek's act except Parashat Zachor; therefore he wondered it is d'oraisa and how the world is lenient. And afterward answers the body of the Torah's positive mitzvah they fulfill through Parashat Vayavo Amalek, only Rabanan enacted to read also Parashat Zachor — and on d'rabbanan there is no question why they are lax. And if so it works for us the world's custom that they fulfill d'oraisa. But for us Rabanan did not enact the remembrance be in Parashat Zachor — he says fine that action d'rabbanan should not precede remembrance d'rabbanan — for d'rabbanan we require remembrance be in Parashat Zachor and not in Parashat Vayavo Amalek; and if so we require action d'rabbanan not precede remembrance d'rabbanan. And further it appears to him: since we hold mitzvot require kavvanah in Torah matters — so too in Parashat Zachor if it were from the Torah we would require intent to fulfill thereby. Per this it comes out fine that Magen Avraham reconciles the world's custom: those who do not come to hear Parashat Zachor — those intend to fulfill through Parashat Vayavo Amalek and fulfill thereby. But for us, since in truth we practice every year to read Parashat Zachor — we intend to fulfill thereby and not through Parashat Vayavo Amalek, and especially since this year they will read Parashat Zachor on the Shabbat after. And know: even Shmuel admits they read Parashat Zachor, only he says they delay and does not say one fulfills through Parashat Vayavo Amalek. And perforce he wanted to fulfill the mitzvah from the preferred way to read Parashat Zachor per Chazal's enactment — and if so now too they will read Parashat Zachor tomorrow; therefore we are concerned they will not intend to fulfill through Parashat Vayavo Amalek for the sake of Parashat Zachor as their way all years — and if they do not intend they will not fulfill again since mitzvot require kavvanah. Therefore again action would precede remembrance; therefore they enacted to read Parashat Zachor first — and it comes out fine. And one may also say simply: since it is written "remembered and done" and from this we derive to precede remembrance to action — we require it be in language of remembrance literally, namely "Remember what Amalek did to you" — not so in Parashat Vayavo Amalek he did not say the mitzvah of remembrance to remember, and the language of "remembered" does not apply to it — understand this. Thus what I answered the aforementioned questioning scholar — examine well.
kaf-hachayyim/6:_: (6) If they erred and read the order of the portions in the first Adar, they must return and read them in the second Adar, as in Megillah 6b — halacha is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel (see there); so too Tur siman 688 per the Hagahot in Beit Yosef s.v. what is written there; Darkei Moshe and Bach there likewise. Rama — in this siman end of gloss 21. I saw in Mishpat if an error fell on gloss 14. In my view siman 9 gloss 14. Sha'ar 8 gloss 96.
